mutations.because: The lane's central requirement: the scene cap is the DOMAIN's rule, called, not counted again in the editor. This replaces the call with the naive local count a reader reaches for, and it is wrong in the two ways `scenesProblem` is careful about — repeats of one scene are ONE scene, and beats naming none spend nothing. A timeline whose six beats all name the same background spends one scene and must be accepted; the count sees six and refuses. This surface previously re-implemented the Set/flatMap under a comment promising it counted 'the same way the domain counts them', which is a promise a copy can only keep until one of them changes.

Clearing must DELETE the key, never write `background: undefined`. The two are the same to `?.` and to a shallow equal, and different to `canonicalJson` — and X33's `hashCopy` serialises `copy.timeline` in full, so the wrong spelling moves `copyHash` for a beat nobody changed and a selective re-roll pinned to the persisted report is refused for it. The observable is the DRAFT, not the projection: `toBrief` already spreads through `isNamedBackground`, so a projected brief looks identical either way — which is why the first draft of this mutation pointed at the byte-identical test and did not reproduce. It points at the draft's own-property assertion instead.
command: deletes the key rather than writing undefined

note: Both mutations were rewritten after the first pair failed to reproduce. #0's `after` had ANDed the naive count in FRONT of the call, so the repeats case still returned undefined and nothing went red; it now replaces the condition. #1 had pointed at the byte-identical projection test, which cannot see the difference because `toBrief` guards with `isNamedBackground`; it now points at the draft assertion. Recording a mutation that cannot fail is the defect the -t liveness gate exists to catch, and verify-manifests caught this one.
